approach: Two root causes, each fixed where it starts. (1) The email allow-list scan ran only in admit(), after the candidate commit was built, so the producer never learned of the address and the refusal named a file but no line. Fix: a line-numbered scan of the snapshot's working diff (new athena-gate fn disallowed_email_lines, reusing disallowed_emails and the configured PersonalData). It is called from producer_loop's self-check (producer.rs) next to `unmet` and `unchanged`. A finding is sent back to the producer as a problem ('<path>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list'), with the send_back_text extended by a section and the finding kept in the attempt's invocation detail. If the address is still present when the single send-back (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1) is used up, the run stops with failure('admission refused the change: <path>:<line> adds ...'), so the producer's own run fails naming file and line and no candidate is built. Admission keeps its own scan as backstop. (2) Earlier-case search: narrow_cases filters CaseRow by class_of_work and category only, newest 5, and never reads an outcome's refusal reason; apply_answer then drops every case not passed in and in the chosen class, so a model that sees none picks 'new' and the record shows new_class=true with empty earlier_cases. Conditions that each produce that: (a) the earlier jobs' cases differ in class_of_work/category; (b) five or more newer unrelated cases in the same bucket crowd them out; (c) the earlier jobs have no CaseRow; (d) records are not where read_records looks (it walks self.git.dir() on disk, while event_of_job and `known` read git). records/ is absent from my copy, so which occurred is not proven; the fix covers a-c and the job_reasons part of d. Fix: Event gains the job's outcome reason; Records gains job_reasons (job id to outcome reason), filled by read_records from outcome files and then overlaid in introspect() from the git-loaded `known` records; narrow_cases lists first the cases whose job's outcome has the same admission refusal key as the event, then class/category matches, capped at CASE_CAP; introspect() flags matching jobs that have no CaseRow. apply_answer is unchanged. One producer.md line and a CHANGELOG entry naming both causes.

decisions.choice: Run the scan inside producer_loop's self-check (producer.rs), as a problem that is sent back (once, PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS), and make it a hard stop if the address is still in the work tree when the send-back is used up. Compute it after `unchanged`, via a helper Athena::working_diff_scan(&self, snapshot) -> Result<Vec<String>> in run/candidate.rs. The loop breaks with a report only when unmet, unchanged and email findings are all empty. The send-back text gets an added section from a new send_back.rs fn `with_address_findings(text, findings)`, so send_back_text's signature and its two callers in run_pin_tests.rs stay unchanged. The findings join `problems`, so they are printed ('producer   sent back: README.md:3 adds ...') and stored in the attempt invocation's detail. On exhaustion, set closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, 'admission refused the change: <findings joined by "; ">') and return Flow::Stop.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1: the request asks for a required check inside the producer loop, and the producer gets the line number while its edits are still in place and can remove the address. The final stop makes the check required rather than advisory: an address that survives the send-back would be refused at admission anyway, so the run fails there with the line and without building the candidate. The 'admission refused the change: ' prefix keeps introspection's matcher seeing the same text as an admission refusal. A scan finding is a hard failure even if unmet criteria also remain, since admission would refuse anyway.

rejected.why: The producer gets no feedback (finding 1); only the line number and skipping the candidate commit improve.

decisions.choice: No-base case: working_diff_scan takes snapshot.base() and, if None, returns the same error change_list gives (GitError::Refused 'this snapshot has no base commit'). In producer_loop this is unreachable in practice, because change_list()? earlier in the same pass already returns that error. The helper therefore adds no new behavior for it.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: matches change_list's behavior (snapshot.rs:200-207) and avoids silently skipping the scan.

decisions.choice: Add disallowed_email_lines in athena-gate content.rs: run `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-renames --no-ext-diff <from> <to>` through Git::run_bytes on the snapshot's Git (snapshot.git(), isolated), parse the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` headers to number added lines, and call the existing disallowed_emails on each. admission.rs wraps it as working_diff_email_violations returning PolicyViolation with the EMAIL_RULE detail prefixed '<path>:<line> '.
decisions.reason: Git::added_lines returns (path, line text) with no line numbers, and the failure must name the line. Counting only added lines keeps an address already in the base from being blamed on the producer. The same disallowed_emails and PersonalData mean one email rule and one allow-list (buy-first).

rejected.option: Scan whole changed files and report line numbers
rejected.why: Would flag addresses already in the base.

rejected.option: Change Git::added_lines to return line numbers
rejected.why: Shared API with other callers; widens the change.

decisions.choice: An in-loop failure starts the retry fresh from the base with the path:line reason in the failure record; no retry-seed work. The test asserts the job closes Failed, not TimedOut.
decisions.reason: tree_seed needs a rejected candidate and resume_seed needs a mark written after the candidate is built, so an admission-refused job gets neither today either. Nothing is lost relative to a refused candidate.

rejected.option: Keep the work tree like keep_timed_out_work
rejected.why: Would close the job as TimedOut and needs a timeout_seed change.

decisions.choice: Event gains reason: Option<String>, set in event_of_job from outcome.reason (None for interventions). Past jobs' reasons come from Records.job_reasons: BTreeMap<String,String>, filled in read_records from outcome files (OutcomeRow gains #[serde(default)] reason), then in introspect() overlaid from the already-loaded git records `known` (known.jobs[job].outcome.reason) through a small pub(crate) fn add_job_reasons(&mut Records, impl Iterator<Item=(String,String)>) that the test also calls. Git wins on a conflict.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. introspect() reads cases with read_records(self.git.dir()) from disk, while event_of_job and `known` read GitRecords::load from git; after the records cutover the outcomes may exist only in git. The overlay makes job_reasons independent of which holds them. Event.reason avoids re-parsing event.what, which mixes title, reason and verification text.

rejected.option: job_reasons from read_records only
rejected.why: Empty (and the fix inert) if outcomes are not on disk (finding 3).

rejected.option: Re-parse event.what
rejected.why: Fragile composed string.

rejected.option: Look up job_reasons[event.job]
rejected.why: Depends on the job's own outcome being on disk.

decisions.choice: refusal_keys(reason) -> Vec<String> in admission.rs keys on admission's own rule stems. admission.rs gains pub const REFUSED_PREFIX = 'admission refused the change: ' and a list of fixed stem constants for the details formatted '{path} <stem>': EMAIL_RULE = 'adds an email address outside the allow-list', 'is under records/, which only Athena writes', 'is private to the repository owner', 'is the owner\'s own document; no job may change it', 'is a submodule or gitlink', and 'bytes, over the limit of' for size. admit() formats its details from these constants (no behavior change). refusal_keys returns [] unless the reason starts with REFUSED_PREFIX; it splits the rest on '; ' and, per segment, returns the first stem the segment contains, and none if no stem matches. Detail text outside the list (classification, configuration, governance) gives no key.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: a path with no '.' or '/' (LICENSE, Makefile) still keys correctly because the key is the stem, not a guess at the path token; size refusals match despite varying byte counts; the in-loop detail '<path>:<line> adds ...' and the admission detail '<path> adds ...' yield the same key. The key is general to admission rules, as the request says 'the admission refusal reason'.

rejected.option: Drop a leading path-like token
rejected.why: Guesses which token is a path and fails on names with no '.' or '/'.

rejected.option: Exact match on the full reason
rejected.why: Stored refusals name different files; would never match.

rejected.why: A new class has no earlier cases by definition; the model picked 'new' only because it was shown none.

decisions.choice: narrow_cases order: first the cases whose job (CaseRow.job) has a job_reasons entry whose refusal keys intersect the event's keys (newest first), then class_of_work+category matches (newest first), de-duplicated by id, truncated to CASE_CAP. The event's keys come from Event.reason. Signature unchanged.
decisions.reason: Refusal matches go first so they cannot be crowded out of the cap (cause b) and match across class/category (cause a). Existing narrowing behavior is unchanged when the event has no refusal key.

rejected.option: Substring-match only the email phrase
rejected.why: Would not cover other admission refusals.

risks.risk: New tests, CHANGELOG and docs contain email-like text, so the scan (or admission) would fail the producer's own run on this change.
risks.mitigation: Build addresses in tests from fragments with concat(). Use only allow-listed forms in the CHANGELOG, or none. The prompt line says 'emails' with no address.

risks.risk: The producer.md line raises the change capability's producer set enough to become the maximum row and make the facts file stale.
risks.mitigation: The line is about 30 tokens against about 146 free. Run cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets; if it fails, report the computed values instead of editing docs/system-facts.md.

risks.risk: Hunk-header parsing mis-numbers lines (zero-add hunks, binary files, odd path characters).
risks.mitigation: Parse only `+c[,d]` of the `@@` header and count only lines starting '+' (not '+++'); skip `+++ /dev/null`; tests for added, modified (two hunks) and deleted files. An unparsable hunk gives no finding, and admission still catches the address.

risks.risk: A send-back used on an address leaves less room for the unmet-criteria send-back, because there is only one (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1).
risks.mitigation: Findings and unmet items share one send-back brief and one problems list, so one pass reports all; the producer sees both.

risks.risk: The refusal key matches unrelated refusals, or refusal matches fill the cap and hide class/category cases.
risks.mitigation: The key is a fixed rule stem, only for reasons with REFUSED_PREFIX. Refusal matches share CASE_CAP with the rest. Tests: a different refusal pulls no cases; the existing narrowing test still passes with reason: None.

risks.risk: An old outcome file lacks `reason` or has extra fields, so read_records fails to parse it.
risks.mitigation: #[serde(default)] on the new field; OutcomeRow does not deny unknown fields.

risks.risk: A retry of an in-loop failure has no kept work.
risks.mitigation: Same as an admission-refused job today (no seed applies); the failure reason carries path:line. Stated in the working_diff_scan doc comment.

risks.risk: Adding the Event.reason field breaks Event literals elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep found Event literals only in introspect.rs (event_of_job, event_of_intervention, in-file tests) and crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs; the producer rechecks with cargo clippy --all-targets.

risks.risk: Changing admit()'s details to use shared constants alters existing admission text and breaks tests or stored matchers.
risks.mitigation: The constants hold the exact current strings; existing admission tests run unchanged and must pass.

The address is built with concat() from fragments so the test source passes the scan. Test A (persists): both Producer turns write README.md with an address outside the allow-list on line 3. Test B (fixed after send-back): the first turn writes the address on line 3 and the second rewrites README.md without it. The tests call athena.ask(...) then athena.go(job, AcceptedBy::User, &Lines).
demonstrations.observes: A: the UI has a line 'producer   sent back: ... README.md:3 adds an email address outside the allow-list'. The job finishes Failed, not TimedOut. The reason starts 'admission refused the change: ' and contains 'README.md:3'. No UI line starts with 'candidate' and no verifier ran. B: the same send-back line appears, then the job Lands. The second producer turn ran (the script's turn count is 2).

The ':3', no-candidate-line and send-back assertions fail. The file compiles on base, so the failure is an assertion.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in introspect.rs's tests module. Records is built from Records::default() plus CaseRow, ClassRow and job_reasons values. Two older cases are in one registered class, and their jobs' outcome reasons are 'admission refused the change: <path A> adds an email address outside the allow-list' and '... <path B> ...', with the event's class_of_work ('code') and category ('failed'). Six newer unrelated same-bucket cases (cause b). A third refusal case with a different class_of_work (cause a). A third job with the same refusal and no CaseRow (cause c). The event's reason is '... <path C>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list'. A path with no '.' or '/' is used for one job. One part writes two outcome files into a tempdir (AnyRecord::Outcome via canonical_path) and asserts read_records fills job_reasons; another calls add_job_reasons with git-sourced pairs and asserts they overlay. Then it asserts narrow_cases returns the refusal-matched cases first (both same-bucket cases and the different-class case), capped at CASE_CAP, with unrelated cases not displacing them. It asserts an event with a different refusal pulls none, and unrecorded_matches returns the uncased job. It passes the narrowed ids to Athena::apply_answer with an Answer that picks the existing class and cites both.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: All four commands exit 0. For the corpus I read case ids (for example Refuse("check_prior_result_and_scope"), Refuse("check_code_survey")) and did not run it. The change touches no reading parser, so I expect no change and cite no result.
demonstrations.fails_without: cargo test fails on the base code plus only the tests, because the criterion 1 and 3 tests fail without the scan and the refusal-key matching. Without the Event.reason edit in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs, clippy --all-targets fails to compile that test. If new tests or the CHANGELOG carried an address outside the allow-list, the scan or personal_data check would refuse the producer's own change.
demonstrations.seam: The production entry points are the cargo commands, run on the workspace; no fake or fixture is injected. The suites are the ones named under criteria 1-4, which exist or are added by steps 2-11. The refusal_corpus target exists (crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs, read).

demonstrations.method: Criterion 1's tests show the earlier refusal and the send-back; criterion 2's test shows an allow-listed address is not refused. The scan calls the existing disallowed_emails with the same PersonalData, so there is no new rule or second allow-list: the refusal moves earlier and gains a line number. The brief's '5% of newly refused readings' is an estimate. records/ is absent from my copy, so I cannot count past admission email refusals, and the producer must not report a measured figure.
demonstrations.observes: The disallowed address is sent back with its line, then refused at the producer stage if it persists; the allow-listed one is not refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the in-loop scan the producer run does not fail at the producer stage; admission refuses later with no line. If the scan used a stricter rule than admission's, the allow-listed test would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: Athena::go with the athena_with/base_script wrapper and FakeTurn.edits; the scan, allow-list, send-back and failure text are production code. The seam exists; the wrapper is added by step 11.

open_questions: records/ is absent from my copy, so I could not read introspection 20261025-074235-4nff or the outcomes of 9e8t and akwq. introspect() reads cases and classes from disk via read_records(self.git.dir()) but jobs from git (GitRecords::load). The plan overlays only job_reasons from git. If the producer finds that self.git.dir() does not hold records/introspections in production, cases would be empty regardless of this fix; it should report that in its output instead of widening the change.
